body.text: 1 evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmiṃ samaye bhagavāṃ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme /

children.text:
3 sati vo bhikṣava araṇyagatānāṃ vā vṛkṣamūlagatānāṃ vā śūnyāgāragatānāṃ vā utpadyeta bhayaṃ vā chambitatvaṃ vā romaharṣo vā /
4 māṃ yūyaṃ tasmiṃ samaye ākārataḥ samanusmarata /
5 iti hi sa bhagavāṃs tathāgato 'rhāṃ samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna
children.translated_text:
3. If, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, for you who have gone to the forest, or who have gone to the foot of a tree, or who have gone to an empty dwelling, there should arise fear, or trembling, or hair-raising dread—
4. you should at that time recollect me in this manner:
5. 'Indeed, that <s>Bhagavat</s> is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>),
the Well-Gone (<s>Sugata</s>), the Knower of the World (<s>Lokavid</s>), the Unsurpassed, the Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed (<s>puruṣadamyasārathi</s>),

children.text:
śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavāṃ /
6 māṃ vas tasmiṃ samaye ākārataḥ samanusmaratāṃ / yad utpatsyate bhayaṃ vā chambitatvaṃ vā romaharṣo vā tat prahāsyate /
7 bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣava
children.translated_text:
the Teacher of Gods and Men, the Awakened One (<s>Buddha</s>), the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavat</s>).'
6. When you recollect me in this manner at that time, whatever fear, or trembling, or hair-raising dread may have arisen—that will be abandoned.
7. In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>,

children.text:
śakro devendro devāsurasaṃgrāme pratyupasthite devāṃs trāyastriṃśān āmantrayati /
8 sati vo māriṣā devāsurasaṃgrāme samabhirūḍhāṇām utpadyeta bhayaṃ vā chambitatvaṃ vā romaharṣo vā /
9 mama vas tasmiṃ samaye vaijayanto dhvajāgraḥ samanusmartavyaḥ / mama vas tasmiṃ samaye vaijayantaṃ dhvajāgraṃ samanusmaratāṃ / yad utpatsyate bhayaṃ vā chambitatvaṃ vā romaharṣo vā tat prahāsyate /
10 evam eva sati vo bhikṣava araṇyagatānāṃ vā vṛkṣamūlagatānāṃ vā śunyāgāragatānāṃ vā utpadyeta bhayaṃ vā chambitatvaṃ vā romaharṣo vā /
11 māṃ yūyaṃ tasmiṃ samaye ākārataḥ samanusmarata / iti hi sa bhagavāṃ yāvad buddho bhagavāṃ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, when the battle between gods and <s>asuras</s> (demons) was at hand, addressed the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) heaven:
8. 'If, O sirs, when the battle between gods and <s>asuras</s> is fully engaged, there should arise for you fear, or trembling, or hair-raising dread—
9. at that time you should recollect my <s>Vaijayanta</s> banner-top. When you recollect my <s>Vaijayanta</s> banner-top at that time, whatever fear, or trembling, or hair-raising dread may have arisen—that will be abandoned.'
10. Even so, if, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, for you who have gone to the forest, or who have gone to the foot of a tree, or who have gone to an empty dwelling, there should arise fear, or trembling, or hair-raising dread—
11. you should at that time recollect me in this manner: 'Indeed, that <s>Bhagavat</s> [is the <s>Tathāgata</s>]... the Awakened One (<s>Buddha</s>), the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavat</s>).'

children.text: the complete text without abbreviation as in paragraph 5 "bhagavāṃs tathāgato ... budddho bhagavāṃ" is attested in SHT 581a r3-6, 596r3-4, Or.15004/79+80rw-z (ed. in BLSF II), 15007/288v1-2 (ed. in BLSF III), 15009/352r4 ed. (in BLSF III)
children.translated_text: [The complete text without abbreviation as in paragraph 5, 'the <s>Bhagavat</s> is the <s>Tathāgata</s>... the Awakened One, the Blessed One,' is attested in SHT 581a r3-6, 596r3-4, Or.15004/79+80rw-z, 15007/288v1-2, 15009/352r4]

children.text:
12 māṃ vas tasmiṃ samaye ākārataḥ samanusmaratāṃ yad utpatsyate bhayaṃ vā chambitatvaṃ vā romaharṣo vā tat prahāsyate /
13 tat kasmād dhetoḥ / sa hi śakro devendraḥ sarāgaḥ sadveṣaḥ samoha aparimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ aparimukto duḥkhād iti vadāmi /
14 bhīru chambī uttrāsī palāyī sa eka
children.translated_text:
12. When you recollect me in this manner at that time, whatever fear, or trembling, or hair-raising dread may have arisen—that will be abandoned.
13. For what reason? For <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, is with passion, with hatred, with delusion; he is not freed from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair—he is not freed from suffering, I say.
14. He is fearful, trembling, terrified, and prone to flight; he

children.text: ā bibhety api chaṃbaty apy uttrās
children.translated_text: at times fears, at times trembles, at times is terrified,

children.text:
ty api palāyaty api /
15 ahaṃ khalu tathāgato loke utpanna arhāṃ samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathi
children.translated_text:
at times takes flight.
15. But I, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, have arisen in the world as an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed, the Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed,

children.text:
śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavāṃ /
16 vigatarāgo vigatadveṣo vigatamohaḥ parimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimukto duḥkhād iti vadāmi /
17 abhīrur acchaṃbī anuttrāsī apalāyī /
18 tasya mama bhikṣava abhīruṇa acchambina anuttrāsina apalāyinaḥ śrotavyaṃ vacanaṃ kartavyaṃ anuśāsanaṃ karaṇīyam idaṃ sthānam iti /
19 idam avocad bhagavāṃ āptamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandam /
20 dhvajāgrasūtraṃ / samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text:
the Teacher of Gods and Men, the Awakened One, the Blessed One.
16. Free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion; freed from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair—freed from suffering, I say.
17. Without fear, without trembling, without terror, without flight.
18. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the words of me who am without fear, without trembling, without terror, without flight are to be heeded; my instruction is to be followed; this is what should be done.
19. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Those <s>bhikṣus</s>, with gladdened hearts, rejoiced in the words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>.
20. <s>Dhvajāgrasūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Banner-Top). Completed.

body.translated_text: 1. Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
